name: American Lotus

facts.how: Seeds raw or roasted; tubers and young leaves cooked
facts.where: Still lakes, oxbows, slow water of East Texas

caution: Harvest only from clean water, and be certain of the plant. A safe and choice water plant when the water is clean. Never eat a wild plant on this guide's word alone. Confirm identity against several sources and learn the look-alikes first.

sections.title: Identification
sections.body: Huge round leaves standing above the water and pale yellow flowers, followed by the famous shower-head seed pod. The only lotus native to the region.

sections.title: In the kitchen
sections.body: The green seeds are a fresh nutty snack and the ripe ones roast like nuts; the starchy tubers cook like a potato and the unfurling young leaves are a cooked green.
